clue.text: Is there a spring in his step?

definitions.text: Is there a spring in his step?

parts.words: Is there a spring in his step?
parts.note: a lively walker has a spring in their step; this person paces the ground with a forked rod hoping to find a spring of underground water

explanation.walkthrough: 'Spring' reads as bounce in a jaunty walk, but it is a source of water, and the step is the dowser pacing a field.
explanation.definitionFit: A dowser searches for underground water sources by walking with a forked hazel twig.

clue.text: Most hot Arab money in US, etc

indicators.note: in places the Arab money pieces inside the word for the US and its allies

parts.note: the US and its allies are the West
Ar is the dictionary abbreviation for Arab or Arabic
M is an abbreviation for money, as in M1, M3 money supply

explanation.surface: A complaint that petrodollars spent in America and Europe are at their hottest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'US, etc' stands for the Western world as a whole, so 'in' places the Arab money inside it. 'Most hot' is a superlative, matching the answer's form.
explanation.definitionFit: The superlative of warm is the highest degree of heat on a mild scale, so 'most hot' fits it.

clue.text: Lofty viewpoint about second of Dennis Potter plays

indicators.note: plays suggests the letters of the playwright's name romp about into a new order
second of picks the second letter of the name Dennis

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A theatre critic's elevated take on the dramas of Dennis Potter, the television playwright.
explanation.walkthrough: 'second of' gives E from Dennis; 'plays' shuffles E with POTTER. Dennis Potter was a British TV dramatist (The Singing Detective), so 'plays' looks like his works rather than the anagram signal; 'about' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The top of a tall tree gives a high vantage point over the land around it.

clue.text: Italian leaves small volume, first from Harrap, in set

indicators.note: in tells us the pieces before it are placed inside the word for a set

parts.note: a radio set, the wireless
I is the abbreviation for Italian (and the country code for Italy)
cc, cubic centimetres, a small measure of volume

indicators.note: first from takes the opening letter of the publisher's name Harrap

explanation.surface: An Italian slim volume, the first title from the publisher Harrap, is set aside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Italian leaves' looks like the definition but 'Italian' gives I; the definition is just 'leaves'. 'in' puts ICCH within the set. Harrap is a British dictionary publisher.
explanation.definitionFit: Radicchio is a red-leaved chicory eaten as salad greens.

clue.text: Figures in cast

parts.note: taken as written
to cast is to throw or put, as in putting the shot

explanation.surface: Numbers appearing in the line-up of a play's cast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Figures' suggests characters in a cast, but here it means data fed into a computer.
explanation.definitionFit: Data entered into a system, numbers fed into a calculation, is called its feed of information.

clue.text: Like some coffee? One moment

explanation.surface: A request to wait a moment while the coffee is made.
explanation.definitionFit: Freeze-dried granules dissolved in water make a quick coffee, and a single moment is likewise a brief point in time.

clue.text: One is about to regret returning to continent

indicators.note: returning means the run of pieces before it is read backwards, as if travelling home

parts.note: a, the indefinite article, means one
taken as written
a is a dictionary abbreviation for about (Latin ante, or approximately)
to rue is to regret

explanation.surface: Someone about to regret going back to the Continent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' turns A+IS+A+RUE (AISARUE) back to front. 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The great landmass comprising Europe and Asia together is treated as a single continent.

clue.text: Piece on Barry, fashionable fellow -

parts.note: a chess piece is a man
on in the sense of concerning, about
Barry is a town in South Wales

explanation.surface: An article on someone called Barry, a stylish chap.
explanation.walkthrough: Barry looks like a man's name but is a town in South Wales: a piece on Barry is a piece about a town.
explanation.definitionFit: A man-about-town is a sociable, stylish man who frequents fashionable parties and clubs.

clue.text: Dummy run in front of boss, excellent start

indicators.note: in front of places the run letter before the word for boss

parts.note: A1, written AI, means first-rate
R is the cricket abbreviation for run
the head is the boss

explanation.surface: A trial run ahead of meeting the boss gets off to an excellent start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'start' places AI (A1, excellent) at the front. 'Dummy run' reads as a rehearsal, but the definition is 'Dummy' alone.
explanation.definitionFit: A dummy is a stupid person, and a featherbrain is another word for one.

clue.text: Perch behind drive mechanism

indicators.note: behind places the word for perch after the word for drive

parts.note: to drive is to push
a perch, rod or pole is an old unit of length

explanation.surface: A fish behind the drive mechanism.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perch' looks like a fish or a bird's roost but is the old length unit, also called a rod or pole.
explanation.definitionFit: A pushrod is the engine part transmitting cam movement to the valves, a piece of mechanism.

clue.text: Act as host-the Queen will for lye can't wait single clues 9

clue.text: Clean room-removing ton's taken about a month

indicators.note: taken about means the shortened room wraps around the month
removing takes one letter out of the word for room

parts.note: an attic is a room in the roof
T is the abbreviation for ton
Sep is the abbreviation for September

explanation.surface: Tidying a room by clearing out a ton of junk took about a month.
explanation.walkthrough: 'removing' drops one T from the room, and 'taken about' wraps what is left round the month. 'a' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Aseptic means free from germs, sterile, as in surgery.

clue.text: Heavenly passage from Tristan?

indicators.note: from, with the question mark, says the letters of the name are worked into something else

explanation.surface: A love-death ascent to heaven from Wagner's Tristan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' and the question mark signal an anagram of TRISTAN. Tristan suggests Wagner's opera, whose lovers find release in death.
explanation.definitionFit: In astronomy a transit is a planet's or moon's crossing of the face of a star or planet.

clue.text: Freely available in Vermont, apparently

indicators.note: in says the answer is a run of letters held inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Something that is apparently freely available in Vermont.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'Freely' as the definition with 'available in' as indicator, but ON TAP means 'freely available' as a whole and 'available' is no hiding signal; 'in' alone is.
explanation.definitionFit: Beer on tap is drawn straight from the cask, so anything on tap is ready whenever wanted.

clue.text: Get used to pitch, hit a beaut

indicators.note: pitch tosses the letters of the following words about

explanation.surface: Getting used to the cricket pitch, a batter hits a beauty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pitch' looks like the cricket ground but is the anagram signal, as in pitching something about.
explanation.definitionFit: To habituate is to accustom someone, or oneself, to something by repetition.

clue.text: Wipe brow with cloth -it gets very hot

indicators.note: wiping rubs and smears, here mixing the letters of the words around it

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Advice to mop the sweat with a rag because things are getting very hot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wipe' looks like the action of mopping a sweaty forehead, but it signals an anagram of BROW and CLOTH; 'with' joins them.
explanation.definitionFit: A blowlamp produces an intensely hot flame for stripping paint or soldering.

clue.text: Lens, the French town, eulogised leaders before taking picture

indicators.note: before puts the French article ahead of the word for a picture
leaders takes the first letters of the two words before it

parts.note: le is the French masculine word for the
a photo is a picture someone has taken

explanation.surface: A lens is praised by the leaders of a French town before a picture is taken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaders' gives T and E from 'town, eulogised', which go in front of LE, though the clue prints 'the French' first.
explanation.definitionFit: A telephoto is a camera lens that magnifies distant subjects.

clue.text: Network Rail finally getting a trophy -cool

indicators.note: finally takes the closing letter of the word rail

parts.note: TT stands for the Tourist Trophy, the Isle of Man motorcycle races
to ice something is to cool it

explanation.surface: Network Rail finally wins a trophy and keeps its cool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Network Rail' reads as Britain's rail-track company, but 'Network' is the definition and 'finally' takes L from 'Rail'.
explanation.definitionFit: A lattice is a criss-cross grid or framework of strips, a network.

clue.text: Stage show

explanation.definitionFit: To stage a play is to put it on before an audience, and to show something is to display or offer it.

clue.text: Area where pop threesome not right

parts.note: pop is a familiar word for father, pa

indicators.note: not drops the letter for right from the word for threesome

parts.note: a trio is a group of three

explanation.surface: A place where a pop band of three isn't quite right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pop threesome' looks like a music trio, but 'pop' is father, PA.
explanation.definitionFit: A patio is a paved area beside a house.

clue.text: Norm, venerable top-class climber

parts.note: par is the standard or norm
Ven is the abbreviation for Venerable, an archdeacon's title
U means upper-class, socially top drawer

explanation.surface: Norm, a revered top-class mountaineer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climber' suggests a mountaineer but means a social climber.
explanation.definitionFit: A parvenu is an upstart who has newly risen in society, a social climber.

clue.text: Catch Ezra with drug apparatus

parts.note: to catch is to trap
Ez is a short form of Ezra, the Old Testament book
E is ecstasy, the drug

explanation.surface: Arresting a man named Ezra along with his drug kit.
explanation.walkthrough: Ezra looks like a man's name but is the Bible book, abbreviated EZ; 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A trapeze is a swinging bar hung from ropes, a piece of gymnastic or circus apparatus.

clue.text: Love a duck! Film's end in colour

parts.note: love is zero, O, in tennis

indicators.note: in places the film's last letter inside the name of the duck

parts.note: a teal is a small duck

indicators.note: end takes the last letter of the word film

explanation.surface: An exclamation of surprise, then a film's ending in colour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Love a duck!' is the British exclamation of surprise (like 'blimey'), but it splits into O, A and TEAL; 'in' puts M inside TEAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Oatmeal is a pale greyish-beige shade, the colour of ground oats.

clue.text: Compound alloy? True

indicators.note: compound means mix together, so the letters are blended anew

explanation.surface: Asking whether a compound alloy is genuine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Compound' sits naturally with 'alloy' as metallurgy, but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A loyal friend is true, faithful and steadfast.

clue.text: Storm out, rant, do nothing

indicators.note: out says the letters are thrown out of order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: Someone storms out, rants, and then achieves nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Storm out' reads as walking off in a temper, but 'Storm' is the definition and 'out' shuffles RANT and DO.
explanation.definitionFit: A tornado is a violent whirling windstorm.

clue.text: Simply futile, changing ends, see?

indicators.note: changing ends swaps the first and last letters of the word for futile

parts.note: futile means vain
Ely is a cathedral city, so a bishop's see

explanation.surface: A futile change of sides, seen simply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changing ends' swaps V and N in VAIN to make NAIV. A see is a bishop's diocese; Ely, in Cambridgeshire, is the crossword's favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: To act naively is to act in an innocent, unsophisticated way, simply.

clue.text: Animal transport expensive, we hear

indicators.note: we hear says the words are what the sound of the answer resembles

parts.note: to row is to transport by boat, and dear means expensive

explanation.surface: Moving an animal costs a lot, so we are told.
explanation.walkthrough: ROW and DEAR said together sound the same as the small Eurasian deer.
explanation.definitionFit: The roe deer is a small Eurasian deer, an animal.

clue.text: Tortoiseshell, perhaps?

parts.note: the word suggests the mottled material used for combs, but read as a tortoise's shell it is the home a reptile carries on its back

explanation.walkthrough: Tortoiseshell suggests a cat's coat or the brown mottled material; read as tortoise + shell it is the house a reptile lives in, and also a zoo building for reptiles.
explanation.definitionFit: A zoo building for snakes, lizards and turtles; a tortoise's shell is the dwelling it carries.
